did_you_know.text: Did you know? Hur is described as the firstborn of Ephrathah and as the “father of Bethlehem,” meaning the ancestor or founder of the family of Bethlehem.
Did you know? Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives, Helah and Naarah; the verses specifically list Naarah’s sons.
Did you know? Jabez is described as more honorable than his brothers, and his name is linked to the pain his mother experienced when giving birth to him.
Did you know? Jabez’s prayer includes requests for blessing, expanded territory, God’s presence, and protection from harm; according to the verse, God granted his request.
Did you know? Joab is called the “father of Ge-harashim,” and the text explains the name by saying that many craftsmen lived there.
Did you know? Among Shelah’s descendants were craftsmen who lived in Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king.
Did you know? Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers are said not to have had many children, and their family did not multiply like the families of Judah.

Did you know? The towns of the descendants of Simeon were listed in the Negev, including Beersheba, Moladah, Ziklag, and Hazar-susim; the text notes that these towns existed until the time of King David.
Did you know? The descendants of Simeon went searching for pasture for their flocks and found a spacious, peaceful, and quiet land where the descendants of Ham had previously lived.

Did you know? Five hundred of the descendants of Simeon went to Mount Seir under the leadership of the four sons of Ishi, struck down the remnant of the Amalekites, and settled there until the time of the writer of the chapter.
